title: Fall of Constantinople

when.label: April – 29 May 1453
when.note: The Ottoman army assembled outside the city in April 1453; the city fell on 29 May.

where.name: Land walls of Constantinople (Istanbul)
where.note: Marker placed on the Theodosian land walls, which the Ottoman army breached.

summary: Ottoman forces under Sultan Mehmed II besieged Constantinople by land and sea and broke through its ancient land walls, ending the Byzantine Empire.
description: By the 1450s the Byzantine Empire had shrunk to Constantinople and the land immediately west of it, and the city's population had fallen to between 40,000 and 50,000. Mehmed II built a fortress on the Bosporus and commissioned the Hungarian gunsmith Urban to cast cannon powerful enough to bring down the city walls.

The Ottoman army assembled outside the city in April 1453. After a siege of several weeks, in which cannon kept up a constant bombardment, the Ottomans breached the land wall and took the city on 29 May 1453.
context: The city's 5th-century land wall, built under Theodosius II, had been one of the leading references for military architecture. After the conquest Hagia Sophia was converted into a mosque.

facts.text: The city fell to Mehmed II on 29 May 1453.
Urban's cannon were brought from Edirne to the outskirts of Constantinople by March 1453.
The Theodosian land wall, begun in the 5th century, was about 6,650 metres long.

uncertain.text: Estimates of the siege's length vary with the start date used; Britannica describes a siege of 55 days.
